summary_of_intent: SIKAEGSHOP's API publishes a remaining-stock count for every product, and the custom_json connector read that number twice while writing it down nowhere queryable: `_availability` reduced it to the word in_stock/out_of_stock, and `enrichment_rows` filed it in the attribute bag as prose. The price row — the durable, per-observation column — was never given it. The PR extracts the read into one `_stock_count()` helper (so `_availability` and the price row derive from the SAME fallback chain), points `_availability` at it with no behaviour change, and passes `stock_quantity=_fmt(_stock_count(product))` into `_row()`. The value rule is explicit `is not None`, never truthiness, precisely so that a PUBLISHED 0 ("none left" — 16 of 87 live products, all with is_active true) lands as 0, while a count the shop never mentioned stays NULL rather than being defaulted to a 0 that would read as sold out. `bool` is excluded because `isinstance(True, int)` is True and this family's sibling keys are flags. No migration, no PAYLOAD_VERSION bump: stock_quantity has been in rowspec (`scrapex/rowspec.py:83`), the header baseline and the `price_observation` table since before this connector existed. It ships a live capture (3 byte-faithful products plus a documented 87-product census) and 8 tests, 5 of which crawl TWICE because a first-ever ingest into an empty database has no open period and cannot exercise the append gate.

findings.evidence:

rationale:
NOT redundant — this is the complementary half of main's 8fe16e6, not a duplicate of it. Evidence for the whole question: main's 8fe16e6 fixed the INGEST gate (`_still_the_same_price`, scrapex/ingest.py:1146-1181) so that a moved stock figure forces an observation append; its own commit message says of MADAR "THE CONNECTOR WAS NOT THE GAP". For SIKAEGSHOP the connector IS the gap, and main has never closed it: `git grep -n stock_quantity origin/main -- scrapex/connectors/custom_json.py` returns only `_availability`'s local read (line 180) and the two enrichment-bag lines (528-529) — no `stock_quantity=` on the price row anywhere — and `git log -S'stock_quantity=' origin/main -- scrapex/connectors/custom_json.py` is EMPTY, meaning that keyword has never existed in this file on main. The PR touches ingest.py not at all, so there is no overlap to duplicate. Landed together they are emitter + consumer: connector fills the cell (custom_json.py:511), ingest lets the row through (ingest.py:1173), price_observation stores it, pricehistory.rebuild_offer derives offer_state from it. Neither half works alone, which is exactly why the PR is red on its own branch and green after the merge.

On the standing rules: nothing is edited or normalised — `_stock_count` returns the published number verbatim and `_fmt` only stringifies it, the same treatment prices get (Rule 1). No _ar/English columns touched (Rule 2). No settings anywhere; test_settings_live_in_the_extension.py is inside the 1712 that passed (Rule 3). No asset version string in the diff at all, so nothing moves backward (Rule 4). No migration added and none edited — the diff is one .py and three test files (Rule 5). No PAYLOAD_VERSION touch, and correctly so: stock_quantity is at scrapex/rowspec.py:83, in contracts/header-baseline.json and in the 36-column PRODUCT_PRICES header already, so the payload shape is unchanged and no generation-ledger entry is owed (Rule 6). Parity trio green (Rule 8). Rule 7 is the strongest part of the PR: the tests bite hard, twice over.

No reverted work: main deleted nothing this diff restores, and the `_availability` refactor is provably behaviour-preserving — the old body derived `qty` from the identical `stock_quantity -> stock -> quantity` chain with the identical `isinstance(qty,(int,float)) and not isinstance(qty,bool)` test, and the new body just calls the extracted helper that does exactly that, keeping the `is_active`/`in_stock` flag fallback and the `qty > 0` branch intact. No overwritten guards, no dropped parameters. No scope creep — every hunk is stock-count work; the rewritten enrichment_rows comment is prose explaining why that bag keeps its OPPOSITE falsy guard, and the `add("stock_quantity", ...)` call itself is byte-identical. No existing test was modified (`git diff --name-status origin/main...HEAD` shows one M and three A), so there is no old-test-being-silenced question to answer. No broken contract: stock is in record_hash (`"stock": _canon_amount(stock_dec)`, ingest.py:752) but deliberately NOT in pricekey.build, so filling this column cannot fabricate a price change on any of the 87 sika offers.

The conditions are the two integration facts, not code changes: (1) the branch MUST be brought up to date with main before landing — I verified that is the whole of the CI failure and that the merge turns 3 failed / 5 passed into 8/8; (2) the four minor findings above should be logged as follow-ups, in particular that the count still has no grid or export column, and that a disappearing count at an unmoved price leaves a stale figure that rebuild_offer resurrects. None of the four blocks the merge, and all four are inherited from or shared with main's existing MADAR fix rather than introduced here.

tests.bite_check: Yes. I copied main's scrapex/reports.py over the merged one (production hunk reverted, both new tests kept) and ran `python -m pytest -q tests/test_reports.py -k "offer_block_comes_before or reorder_lost_no_column"`. test_the_offer_block_comes_before_the_filing FAILED with `AssertionError: a classification column is ahead of Price again, which is what made its position depend on how many levels a source publishes / assert 5 > 32` — it bites, and its message names the defect. test_the_reorder_lost_no_column PASSED with the fix reverted, i.e. it does not bite on this change at all. I restored the merged file and both pass again; `git status --porcelain` was empty before I removed the worktree.

rationale:
The reorder itself is correct and lands cleanly: the key set, the labels and the per-source presence gates (including the USD-estimate leak guard, which is set-based in column_presence) are provably unchanged, grid.js reads column order from the server payload and hardcodes only key-based formatters, so no column disappears and the JS/Python contract is untouched. But two halves are missing.

First, this is a revert disguised as a feature. Commit d9e6f7a deliberately replaced hand-typed category_l1..l4 tuples with a generated `*_level_columns()` and wrote down why; PR #63 types twenty of them back in and orphans the generator. I demonstrated the cost: with CATEGORY_LEVELS = 11 — the change reports.py:593 still calls "one line" — the export and the bilingual pair table grow a Category L11 that the table and the manage-columns list never get, and all 1707 tests pass. The reorder did not require this; `*_level_columns(),` inside the filing block yields the identical list.

Second, only one of three consumers moves. ensure_fields is documented never to rewrite an existing dataset_field row, so on a warehouse whose sources have been opened once the Choose-Columns panel and the Current-View export keep the pre-PR order while the grid takes the new one — I measured price at index 5 in the grid and 32 in both the panel and the current-view export on the same simulated warehouse, and 5/5/5 on a fresh one. Migration 0040 is the precedent for the re-seed this PR omits.

Third, the PR changes an owner ruling by code and test while leaving two written statements of the old ruling in place — reports.py:582-585 and docs/data-page-schema.md, which describes itself as the ruling. And of the two new tests only one bites; the other is green with the fix fully reverted and cannot catch the loss the PR itself introduces.

To approve I would want: `*_level_columns()` restored inside the filing block (or CATEGORY_LEVELS retired properly, not left half-live); a migration or re-seed that brings dataset_field.display_order in line, with a test that seeds the old order and asserts the panel and the current-view export agree with the grid; reports.py:582-585 and docs/data-page-schema.md rewritten to state the new ruling; and test_the_reorder_lost_no_column strengthened to compare BROWSE_COLUMNS against the CATEGORY_LEVELS-generated family in both directions instead of asserting the literal 50.

verdicts.finding_summary: blocking / half-shipped — the new title on .dataset-choice-state is a strict PREFIX of the visible freshness line, so the `· N rows seen` tail that text-overflow:ellipsis cuts off is unrecoverable ( _source_list.html:46 )
verdicts.why: I merged origin/fix/the-freshness-line-stops-crushing-the-name onto origin/main in my own worktree and rendered /data through the same TestClient fixture as tests/test_workspace.py. The prefix observation is literally true: title="Last crawled 2026-08-01 10:45 UTC" vs visible "Last crawled 2026-08-01 10:45 UTC · 1 rows seen". But the failure scenario built on it does not happen. I served the merged CSS (tokens.css + components.css + webui.css + pages/data-workspace.css) with the real card DOM and measured in a real browser at 1280x800: the .dataset-choice-detail content box is 315.47px — exactly the width the finding names — and the longest realistic caption measures scrollWidth 262px ("Last crawled 2026-07-30 10:15 UTC · 19,548 rows seen"), 269px for the `· 1,234,567 requests` form, 282px even for `· 19,548,000 rows seen`. All under 315px, so element.scrollWidth == clientWidth and truncated == false. The line is NOT ellipsised on desktop at all; the screenshot the finding describes ("paints as Last crawled 2026-07-30 10:15 UT…") cannot be produced at that width. Truncation only begins below a ~345px viewport, and at the 320px viewport the finding itself cites the clip lands at 237px — I measured "Last crawled 2026-07-30 10:15 UTC · 19,548" at 211px and "… 19,548 rows" at 237px, so even there the 19,548 figure is still painted; only the trailing word is clipped. The claim "the 19,548 figure is unreachable by any means" is therefore false. Both halves of the fix (title attribute in _source_list.html and the ellipsis rule in data-workspace.css) are present in the merged tree, so the "half-shipped" category does not apply either. What remains is a cosmetic incompleteness: the title could have carried the whole line. No source truth is edited (rule 1 intact — the title is a subset, never a rewritten value), and the two new tests in tests/test_vendor.py bite: I replaced data-workspace.css and _source_list.html with `git show origin/main:` versions and both tests fail (IndexError on the missing rule / missing title=), then pass again on the merged tree. Full suite green (all tests pass, incl. tests/test_vendor.py, test_webui.py, test_workspace.py, test_settings_live_in_the_extension.py — 149 passed for those four). `python -c "import scrapex"` resolved inside my worktree, so no PYTHONPATH override was needed.

verdicts.finding_summary: major / test-does-not-bite — tests/test_vendor.py:1062 asserts grid-row:1 inside `.dataset-choice>.source-identity-meta{…}`, a selector that matches zero elements
verdicts.why: The factual core is correct and I reproduced it, but the severity is inflated by two levels. scrapex/webui/templates/_source_identity.html:37-40 wraps the badge as .source-identity > .source-identity-footer > .source-identity-meta, and _source_list.html:28-55 shows .dataset-choice's only direct children are that .source-identity and .dataset-choice-detail. My rendered /data dump confirms it. `grep -rn source-identity-meta` over the whole tree (including extension/ and design/) shows no other producer puts it as a direct child of .dataset-choice; extension/app.js:380 builds the same nested shape. So data-workspace.css:53 is indeed dead and the PR's added `grid-row:1` on it is a no-op. However: (a) the dead rule is NOT introduced by this PR — `git log -S'.dataset-choice>.source-identity-meta'` dates it to 022793d/34ec24c, and the footer wrapper that orphaned it landed later in fe719fb, so this is pre-existing debt on main, not a regression; (b) the test as a whole DOES bite, which is what rule 7 requires — with main's data-workspace.css restored, test_the_dataset_freshness_line_does_not_crush_the_name fails on the `grid-column:1/-1` assertion, which is the assertion that actually guards the fix; (c) the vacuous line 1062 cannot mask any regression this PR could cause — the caption is pinned to grid-row:2 explicitly, so it cannot be auto-placed back beside the identity regardless. Nothing on screen is wrong, nothing behaves wrong, and no test lies about a passing state. This is one redundant assertion plus one dead CSS rule: worth deleting, not worth blocking a merge.

verdicts.finding_summary: major / stale-assumption — the nine-line comment at data-workspace.css:54-59 (repeated in tests/test_vendor.py:1046-1052) blames column 2 as "the narrow auto-width column the [Row N] badge lives in", but the badge never lived in column 2
verdicts.why: The narrow factual point holds: the badge renders inside .source-identity, which data-workspace.css:52 pins to grid-column 1, so the parenthetical in the comment describes the *intent* of the dead rule at line 53 rather than what the browser did; the actual occupant of column 2 on main was .dataset-choice-detail. I verified this from the rendered DOM and from main's version of the file. But this is a prose inaccuracy inside a comment, not a defect: it changes no behaviour, no test outcome, and no rendered output. The comment's operative sentence — that the freshness caption was in column 2, inflated that auto track and starved minmax(0,1fr) — is correct, and that is the part a maintainer acts on. The stated failure scenario is entirely hypothetical ("the next maintainer... either (a) or (b)"), and the comparison to the lag-guard incident is rhetorical: the lag guard was executable code returning false verdicts, whereas this is a code comment that cannot lie to a test runner. Downgrading to nit; the correct remedy is to delete the dead rule at line 53 and trim the parenthetical, which is the same one-line cleanup finding #2 asks for.

findings.summary: The new section specifies a whole per-backend settings surface without once naming the Chrome extension as its home, contradicting the settings standing rule the repo enforces with a test.
findings.evidence: `sed -n '265,478p' docs/MASTER-PLAN.md | grep -niE "extension|chrome|side panel"` -> NONE, across all 214 added lines. Yet §8.5 requires "Each backend should have a health state, installed and certified versions, licence/notice view, disk footprint, last compatibility test, update channel, logs, and an explicit uninstall path", and §8.6 requires "3. **Expert** - backend-specific settings generated from the adapter schema, with a raw pass-through escape hatch where safe." §8.1 additionally constrains "the existing settings screen" without saying which surface that is. The enforcing guard exists: tests/test_settings_live_in_the_extension.py (62 lines) is present on main and in the merged tree.
findings.failure_scenario: An implementer reads §8.5/§8.6, builds the Engine Manager and Expert settings panes into the Jinja web UI (which the document elsewhere calls "exactly one primary UI to retrofit", line 210), and trips tests/test_settings_live_in_the_extension.py - the rule that all settings live in the extension and the web page is display-only appears nowhere in the 216 new lines.

findings.summary: The proposed adapter artifact contract enumerates its fields and includes no language or locale dimension, in a project whose second standing rule is bilingual capture.
findings.evidence: `sed -n '265,478p' docs/MASTER-PLAN.md | grep -niE "arabic|bilingual|_ar\b|language|locale"` -> NONE. §8.4 lists the contract exhaustively: "Final artifacts should carry at / least canonical URL, requested/final URLs, timestamp, HTTP evidence, MIME type, / content hash, raw-artifact reference, parent/discovery evidence, and backend / provenance." Nothing marks which language a captured value is in, and §8.3 assigns Crawl4AI "Clean Markdown/documents and AI/RAG-oriented extraction" as a role without restating that captured text may not be transformed.
findings.failure_scenario: A first spike shapes the adapter contract from this list, ships without a language marker, and an Arabic page and its English alternate arrive as two artifacts indistinguishable at the contract boundary - the point at which the unmarked-is-English / _ar-is-Arabic rule can quietly be lost or the two merged.

findings.summary: Section 8.1 forbids overloading the word 'engine', then section 8.5 names the crawler-backend installer 'Engine Manager'.
findings.evidence: §8.1 (docs/MASTER-PLAN.md:289-291): "The current plan uses **engine** to mean a data-domain capsule. External crawlers / must not overload that word". §8.5 (docs/MASTER-PLAN.md:380-381): "The possible product shape is an **Engine Manager** that installs isolated, / version-pinned packs on demand" - and every pack it lists (Python pack, Browser pack, Discovery pack, Archive pack, Provider adapters) is a Crawler Backend, not a Domain Engine.
findings.failure_scenario: The section's own rule is broken by the section's own naming, so the first reader to implement it inherits the ambiguity it was written to prevent: an 'Engine Manager' menu that manages crawler backends sits next to a Domain Engine concept that also calls itself an engine.

rationale:
The PR-specific brief's hypothesis is confirmed. This is a docs-only change: 216 added lines in docs/MASTER-PLAN.md and nothing else. Merged onto today's main it produces zero conflicts, and every CI step re-run on the merged tree is green (1704 passed / 1 xfailed under the default path; 1697 passed / 1 xfailed / 7 skipped under CI's SCRAPEX_FULL_MIGRATIONS=1; parity 8/8, 5/5, 3/3; 13/13 extension; 13/13 apps_script; manifest OK; panel gate 73). No test, no source file, no CI step and no lint config reads the file the PR touches, so the red checks cannot originate here - they are inherited from a base that is 10 commits behind, and merging clears them. I could not reproduce the two failures on the stale base either (Windows/Python 3.14 vs CI's ubuntu/3.12), and I say so rather than claim a diagnosis I did not observe.

I checked the repository's named accident patterns and found none of them. Reverted work: the diff has exactly two deleted lines, the renumbered heading and the closing paragraph, which is re-added byte-identical apart from a trailing newline - no line main deleted on purpose is restored, no version or number is lowered, no asset version is touched. Overwritten features: no function exists in the diff. Half-shipped: no caller, template hook, emitter or consumer is added - the only two-halves breakage is documentary (BACKLOG's §8 cross-references, finding 2). Duplicated solution: `grep -rliE 'scrapy|crawlee|crawl4ai|firecrawl|katana|heritrix' docs/ *.md` matches only MASTER-PLAN.md itself, so nothing in main already covers this. Broken contract: BROWSE_COLUMNS, grid.js, PAYLOAD_VERSION, the generation ledger, the migration streams and the parity trio are all untouched, and parity is green. Scope creep: one file, one topic. Tests that do not bite: the PR neither adds nor changes a test, and the change is not behavioural.

The conditions are two small, concrete edits, neither of which blocks merge. First, §8.2's single 'Non-negotiable invariant' names `harvest.db` - a file main's own scrapex/db.py:30-35 documents as empty since 21 July and explicitly NOT the warehouse - so the one hard commitment in an otherwise-hedged section protects the wrong path; it should name marketlens.db and general.db, and the surrounding 'the one append-only ScrapeX warehouse' should acknowledge the two-database split. Second, docs/BACKLOG.md:237 and :466 still describe MASTER-PLAN's §8 as the Open Decisions section that this PR moved to §9; both lines were present in the author's own base, so this is an oversight rather than a stale-base collision, and both are one-word fixes. The remaining findings (Topology B grounding versus the file's own recorded Topology A decision, the Engine Manager naming that breaks §8.1's own rule, and the absence of any mention of the extension-settings rule or of the bilingual capture rule in 214 lines of design text) are worth an editing pass before anyone treats this section as a plan, but the section labels itself exploratory and revisable and none of it executes.
